quote: If you want to understand Gen X, just remember TV once had to remind a whole generation of parents to go find their kids.
caption: My daughter asked me last week what I did after school when I was eleven. I told her the truth. I got off the bus at 3:15, let myself in with the key on a shoelace around my neck, ate a sleeve of saltines standing up, and left. Where did you go, she asked. Out. With who. Whoever was outside. When did you come home. When the news came on, or when I got hungry, whichever came first. She looked at me like I had survived a shipwreck. I didn't have the heart to tell her it was the best part of the day.
first: My mother's entire tracking system was opening the back door and yelling my name once. If I didn't answer, she assumed I was fine and went back to her show. I was always fine. I have no idea how, but I was always fine.

quote: Dating in midlife is something else. Half the people are still sorting out their baggage. The other half are the reason everyone has baggage. I’m staying in.

Then in the first nine minutes he told me about his ex-wife, his other ex-wife, the woman he almost married in 2009, and a lawsuit involving a boat. He asked nothing about me. Not one thing. When he went up for a refill I sat there doing math on how many more ex-wives might be coming. I finished my coffee, thanked him kindly, and drove straight home to my couch. Carol has been informed.

quote: Nothing kills the joy of sinking into bed like suddenly realizing you forgot to pee.
caption: Last night I did everything right. Teeth brushed, lamp off at 10:20, the good pillow flipped to the cold side, blanket tucked under both feet exactly the way I like it. The cat settled on my legs. My whole body let out the long sigh it saves for the end of the day. Then, about forty seconds into true happiness, my bladder cleared its throat. I lay there and negotiated. I told it we could wait until morning. It said we could not. So the blanket came off, the cat was offended, and the whole ritual started over from scratch.

quote: I used to wonder why dishwasher pods have to say “Do not eat.” Then I met people.
caption: At the neighborhood potluck on Sunday, a grown man in a golf shirt picked up a decorative pinecone off the table and asked if it was the dessert. He was serious. His wife had to take it out of his hand. Ten minutes later a woman two houses down explained to me that she doesn't wear sunscreen because she has a base tan from 1994. Then someone microwaved a foil pan. I stood by the punch bowl and quietly made my peace with every warning label I've ever laughed at. They know exactly who they're writing for. I've met him. He took a pinecone.

quote: My brain lets go of names, appointments, and why I walked in here. But every word of “Pour Some Sugar on Me” is perfectly preserved.
caption: On Thursday I walked into the garage, stood there for a full minute, and walked back out with nothing. I still don't know what I went in for. That same afternoon I ran into a woman I've known for twelve years at the pharmacy and called her Linda. Her name is Brenda. Then the dentist's office called to ask where I was, and the answer was the pharmacy, calling Brenda Linda. On the drive home the radio played one song from 1988 and I sang every single word, both verses, the bridge, the ad-libs. My memory works fine. It just has priorities.
